concept.tagline: Scoring device posture, ASN/GeoIP, and TLS fingerprints in real time to step up risky logins to phishing-resistant WebAuthn/FIDO2.
concept.purpose: Understand why SMS/TOTP fall to Adversary-in-the-Middle (AiTM) proxies, how WebAuthn binds to rpId, and how risk engines balance security with friction.

spark.summary: Risk-based Multi-Factor Authentication (RBA) evaluates contextual telemetry—device posture, ASN/GeoIP, impossible travel, and TLS fingerprints—in real time to dynamically step up high-risk logins to phishing-resistant WebAuthn/FIDO2 while keeping trusted sessions frictionless.
spark.keyTakeaway: Static SMS/push MFA fails against AiTM reverse-proxy phishing and push bombing; pair a <50 ms risk-scoring engine with origin-bound FIDO2/WebAuthn passkeys and number-matched push fallback.
spark.byteSummary:
**Core Mechanics:** **Risk-Based Authentication (RBA)** evaluates contextual signals at login time in **<50 ms**—device posture/cookie, IP reputation (Tor/VPN/residential proxy ASN), impossible travel (>800 km/h), and JA4 TLS fingerprint—and routes.

**Visual & Structural Flow:** Depicts Real-Time Risk Scoring & Authentication Decision Tree (LOW RISK (0-29) -> MEDIUM (30-69) -> HIGH (70-100)); Why WebAuthn Defeats Evilginx Reverse-Proxy Phishing (User Browser -> evil-login.com -> corp-idp.com).

**Trade-Offs & Production:** Compare MFA factors across phishing resistance, UX, and recovery complexity. Even with WebAuthn, a stolen session cookie (`Set-Cookie`) can be replayed from another machine.

**Failure Modes & Application:** Connect adaptive MFA to OAuth2/OIDC flows, JWT validation, and zero-trust service authentication.

learningJourney.title: What is Risk-Based MFA (RBA) & WebAuthn
learningJourney.explanation:
**Risk-Based Authentication (RBA)** evaluates contextual signals at login time in **<50 ms**—device posture/cookie, IP reputation (Tor/VPN/residential proxy ASN), impossible travel (>800 km/h), and JA4 TLS fingerprint—and routes to frictionless SSO, number-matched push, or **FIDO2/WebAuthn** step-up.

**FIDO2/WebAuthn** signs a server challenge using a hardware/passkey private key cryptographically bound to the exact TLS origin (`rpId`), neutralizing reverse-proxy phishing.

sectionDiagram.summary: Trusted corporate devices stay frictionless while anomalous sessions trigger origin-bound FIDO2 step-up.

learningJourney.title: Why AiTM Phishing Proxies and Push Bombing defeat legacy MFA
learningJourney.explanation:
Credential stuffing and **Adversary-in-the-Middle (AiTM)** phishing proxies (e.g., Evilginx) relay passwords, SMS OTPs, and TOTP codes in real time, stealing the resulting `Set-Cookie` session token.

Meanwhile, **MFA Fatigue (Push Bombing)** floods a victim's phone with push prompts until they tap Approve by mistake.

sectionDiagram.title: Why WebAuthn Defeats Evilginx Reverse-Proxy Phishing
sectionDiagram.summary: The browser signs the actual address-bar origin; an AiTM proxy on a lookalike domain cannot forge a valid rpId signature.

benefits: Protects OIDC/SAML gateways, admin consoles, and financial transfers without punishing known MDM devices.
costs: Must maintain offline break-glass recovery keys for P0 datacenter outages.

benefits: Use short-lived OIDC workload identity tokens, SPIFFE/mTLS certificates, or asymmetric JWTs.
costs: Interactive MFA cannot run in headless automated pipelines.

learningJourney.title: Deterministic Risk Evaluation & Number-Matched Push Fallback
learningJourney.explanation: Evaluate ASN, impossible travel, and device trust in <50 ms, enforce WebAuthn `rpId` verification, and cap push attempts (e.g., max 3 per 15 min) with 2-digit number matching.
learningJourney.purpose: Operational control: configure bounds, failure handling, and safe production defaults.

learningJourney.title: Alternatives: FIDO2/WebAuthn vs. Number-Matched Push vs. TOTP/SMS
learningJourney.explanation: Compare MFA factors across phishing resistance, UX, and recovery complexity.

benefits: Origin-bound (immune to AiTM phishing), zero server shared secrets, one-tap biometric UX.
costs: Requires cross-device passkey sync or hardware backup keys for lost-device recovery.

benefits: Defeats blind MFA fatigue bombing by requiring the user to type a 2-digit screen code.
costs: Still vulnerable to social-engineered real-time AiTM proxies if the user reads the code aloud/into a proxy.
Vulnerable to SIM swapping (SMS) and real-time AiTM phishing relays (both).

learningJourney.purpose: The trade-off: compare competing approaches across latency, consistency, and operational cost.

learningJourney.title: Device-Bound Sessions (DBSC) + Offline Break-Glass
learningJourney.explanation: Even with WebAuthn, a stolen session cookie (`Set-Cookie`) can be replayed from another machine. Modern IdPs pair WebAuthn with **Device Bound Session Credentials (DBSC)** / mTLS token binding and keep hardware-key **break-glass admin accounts** outside the risk engine.

ideas.description: Mobile carriers rotate CGNAT IPs across cities; weight device-bound cookies and JA4 TLS fingerprints higher than raw GeoIP city hops.

knowledgeCheck.question: Why is FIDO2/WebAuthn immune to Adversary-in-the-Middle (AiTM) reverse-proxy phishing attacks like Evilginx?

options.text: It rotates 6-digit codes every 5 seconds instead of 30 seconds
options.feedback: Faster TOTP rotation does not stop a real-time reverse proxy from relaying the code.

options.text: The browser cryptographically binds the assertion signature to the exact address-bar TLS origin (rpId), which fails validation on the attacker's lookalike domain
options.feedback: Correct: because the clientDataJSON origin does not match the real IdP rpId, the IdP rejects the signature.

options.text: It disables TLS encryption during login
options.feedback: WebAuthn requires a valid HTTPS/TLS origin.

_recommendedProblem.title: Active-Active Multi-Master Split-Brain Recovery
_recommendedProblem.prompt: Redesign an active-active multi-master relational replication pipeline between us-east-1 and eu-west-1 (6,000 writes/sec, 85 ms WAN RTT, < 15 ms p99 local commit) so a 9-minute transatlantic partition and 180-250 ms NTP clock skew never cause silent Last-Write-Wins (LWW) overwrites.
